pairs.subject: authoring-block-vocabulary
pairs.evidence: src/components/guide/blocks/FeatureHighlight.tsx:16 The `:::feature` block passes an authored `color=` value straight into an inline style (14 corpus uses across en and every locale), and the locale-parity gate compares only the sequence of block types; that breaks closure (appearance is set in content) and leaves item counts, enum labels and anchors unchecked across locales.

techniques.evidence: src/components/guide/blocks/FeatureHighlight.tsx:16 Most of this is done well: one dispatch, KNOWN_DIRECTIVES derived from GRAMMAR (parseGuide.ts:311), and an unknown name renders nothing while a diagnostic fails the build (parseGuide.ts:418). But the feature grammar captures `color=(\S+)` (parseGuide.ts:207) and the renderer applies it as a raw style. That is the style pass-through the technique names as an escape hatch to refuse.

src/components/guide/guide-markdown/parseGuide.ts:287 Each block has its own line grammar. Continuation lines fold into the previous item, but a line shaped like a label is reported instead of folded. The dash separator is accepted as a class (DASH, line 126). A skipped line becomes an ignored-line diagnostic, and a block with no usable items becomes an empty-block diagnostic; the gate counts both.

src/components/guide/guide-markdown/parseGuide.ts:56 Each label set is declared once as a const tuple. The grammar admits only those literals, case-insensitively. Style tables are typed as Record<CalloutVariant>/Record<CardStatus>, so a missing entry is a compile error (Callout.tsx:17). Only `warning` escalates to role=alert. Small gap: the on-screen label text ('Tip', 'Roadmap', 'Coming soon') is hardcoded English rather than resolved per locale.

scripts/check-guide-content.mjs:160 The gate does parse the real locale bodies with the renderer's parser, but it compares only the block-type sequence. Item count per block, enum label per item position and the anchor set are not compared, and existing divergences are frozen in a baseline file. BLOCK_TYPES (line 155) is also a hand-kept copy of the node vocabulary.

src/app/guide/[category]/[topic]/page.tsx:121 The HowTo JSON-LD, the TOC (headingsOf) and search (sectionsOf) all re-read the same parsed tree the renderer uses. Emitted step text goes through stripInline (page.tsx:34) so it matches what the reader sees. A body with no steps emits no steps.
